Top candidates: **Charcoal_Rot** (microsclerotia giving charcoal-sprinkled appearance) and **Diaporthe** (black pycnidia in linear rows on stems).

**Analysis:**

- **Test image**: Microscopic view of pale/cream-colored stem tissue with numerous tiny black specks scattered across the surface in a random, diffuse pattern.
- **Charcoal_Rot reference**: Shows bleached/gray stems with tiny black microsclerotia scattered throughout — matches the test image very well (pale tissue + scattered black dots).
- **Diaporthe reference**: Shows darker stem tissue with black pycnidia typically in linear rows, more organized pattern — doesn't match the scattered, random distribution in test image.
- **Anthracnose reference**: Shows dark pods/stems with large irregular lesions and crowded acervuli with spines — clearly different.

The test image is a close-up microscopic view showing the characteristic "charcoal-sprinkled" appearance of **Charcoal_Rot** — tiny black microsclerotia scattered across bleached pale stem tissue, exactly as described in the symptom description.
